item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
{manifests again in response to PM}

Okay, this is going to be a bit of a back-and forth dialogue if you really want to forge this idea into shape, but since you seem serious about it let's dig in:

+ sculpture is still under the rock
- more chiseling

one of the critiques that I get here is that the one ability I do mention (instantly knowing things about stuff he sees) is boring/uninteresting or broken.

To put it simply, they're right. That can be fixed, though.

Firstly, heed Quadraginta's critique in particular- the traits they're pointing to are part of that Edgelord Canyon I mentioned you're trying to tightrope across. You might never win them over, but they're pointing out a lot of the pitfalls you need to avoid. (De-emphasizing the middle name to an initial is a good first move, for instance- was going to mention that being a little on-the-nose in the previous critique myself and forgot.)

Two things in your reply above sort of… bracket both what I've actually been finding interesting about this guy and what you'll want to avoid. I think it might be backwards from what you're thinking, though:

It's not going to be a batman utility belt scenario.

This is actually the less important of the two things, but Batman and his utility belt are a really good example to follow for this guy's collection of anomalies.

We're never told explicitly what's in the utility belt, and with Batman's resources and skills the options are pretty much limited only by what can plausibly fit in the belt. What good Batman writers figure out, though, is that the utility belt is boring when Batman has a gadget that does anything he needs to do for him. Used at its best, the belt always has what Batman needs to do anything in the most interesting way possible.

Same thing here: even you as the writer don't need to know every item Twist has. He can have whatever you want him to have- so long as it's in the name of doing something in the most interesting way possible. That's why I suggested emphasizing that most of his collection are innocuous and/or useless seeming items- they're things that only he would see the potential in. It's boring if he has a gizmo that lets him fly. It's interesting if he combines three minor anomalies in an way that causes him to be hurled through the air havok-physics-glitch style.

I haven't mentioned them because they aren't crucial to the story or to what the story is supposed to be focusing on, which is supposed to be about the SCP foundation trying to get information out of Twist and figuring out the rules to obtaining this information.

Again, the power isn't the interesting part, and the whole "the Foundation NEEDS the information" thing is a bit of a site cliche with oracles. (They might like to have said information, but there's loads of other POIs they'd love to put under a microscope, too.) I'd actually even suggest toning it down further, so that he doesn't have instant absolute insight into everything- if he just gets incomplete flashes and glimpses of insight its both a great narrative tool for foreshadowing and "how we got here" storytelling, and a much less "game-breaking" power.

Vincent Anderson of Anderson Robotics might be a good bit of site lore to look at regarding one way you could approach telling this guy's story. He's a literal cyborg sorcerer with all the makings of a stereotypical edgelord OC by the end of his arc- but his messy, complicated story about a man trying to find an offramp on that road paved with good intentions makes him one of the most interesting characters on the site. In Twist, you've got a similar chance to show us a really simple, fairly weak precognitive/clairvoyant type power leading a guy down the road to become one of the SCPverse's many boogymen.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
you're going about it wrong. If you want to keep the article mysterious, that makes sense. It does not make sense to keep the idea post mysterious.

The purpose of the greenlighting process is to convince at least two authors that you can communicate your idea in a compelling manner.

So… I am not concerned that you would not explain the aura in the idea post, I am concerned that it seems to have no connection to the anomalies as presented. I feel like you missed the point of my critique.

I think you need to sit down and simplify, make a cohesive anomaly about the one man and focus on his anomalous aspects that thematically connect to each other.

When I said this ^ it was not to suggest anything but that your idea felt too disjointed and you should simplify the core anomaly to make more cohesive sense.

You need to develop a cohesive proposal for the idea to communicate what your story is about.

No one is going to greenlight your concept without you explaining the concept. If you choose to withold and say something like "you'll learn about it in the article" I wouldn't trust that this will turn into an article that could survive.

He's not an all-knowing unstoppable monster… just a man who sees a little more than others, with an obsession that may or may not be justified, and a few tricks up his sleeve.

This is a part of the vibe that I am trying to create. In a one on one scenario, Twist can be very intimidating. However, put a couple more people in the room and he is far less deadly and easier to contain due to the nature of how his anomalous traits work, which I planned to explain in the article.

What if he can see the potential in things, too?

The short answer would be yes. So long as the object is within his line of sight, he can view this.

A laundry list of abilities isn't going to interest the audience

I completely agree. Anything he has in his arsenal I already have inventoried. It's not going to be a batman utility belt scenario. I have some stories in mind for this character within the SCP universe with a few of them focusing on how he got some of his artifacts. However, one of the critiques that I get here is that the one ability I do mention (instantly knowing things about stuff he sees) is boring/uninteresting or broken. He does have other capabilities that I haven't mentioned here, but I haven't mentioned them because they aren't crucial to the story or to what the story is supposed to be focusing on, which is supposed to be about the SCP foundation trying to get information out of Twist and figuring out the rules to obtaining this information. So, to placate the critique of "uninteresting anomalous ability", I mentioned a few other items/powers. In response to your review in particular though, I have since removed them.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM Request.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

I'm going to keep this relatively simple, short and concise here. He feels 100% like a generic dark, mysterious, edgy anime character with nothing interesting going on at all whatsoever.

Twist is unable to answer specific questions. When he tries to, an anomalous event occurs that blurs his face and distorts his voice to be unrecognizable and indecipherable.

That's way too convenient and forced for its own good.

Twist can instantly know the purpose, function, and method of elimination for any target he sees. The SCP Foundation NEEDS this intel.

This isn't as physically combatively overpowered as Abel, but by sheer function, this already renders him far, far too overpowered and X-Men-ish for his own good.

Anomalous Properties

I think you mean superpowers, because that's essentially what this guy has here.

And last but not least, and this is admittedly an extremely shallow nitpick: I don't like his name. James DEVILian (Devil?) Twist. The words 'Devil' and 'Twist' are in his name. It really doesn't get any more anime edgey than that.

I apologise if this came off as extremely harsh, but I'm not feeling this at all in the slightest.

I'm also not really a fan of edgy anime characters, so I was kinda…completely the wrong person to crit this.

I also completely forgot to cover the plot here, basically because it doesn't have one.

The core plot of this article is the SCP foundation's various attempts to uncover secret information that Twist holds.

This explains literally nothing. He has secrets. What are those secrets? You can make them secretive if you manage to get to drafting this, but for the idea pitch, please give us more information on what those secrets are.

Yeah, I'm sorry if this disappoints, but I have nothing to offer here in terms of suggestions or recommendations or tips. I can only state what I disliked about this piece, and it was essentially all of it. I deeply apologise for that.

I do hope you stay and pursue a work on this site, though, as the Greenlight process can be brutal. Don't be discouraged. The trip to one's first SCP is worth the struggle.

Anywho, I bid you a good day. 👍

P.S. I didn't even acknowledge the crosslink idea. Here's the most generally agreed upon consensus for crosslinking on one's first SCP: don't. Many would view it as trying to ride off the success of more popular articles. You'll need to be a lot more familiar with how things go here first before crosslinking will become a good idea. A first SCP has to be able to stand on its own.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
(This started as a reply above, but jumping down to a new chain so it's not so horizontally compressed.)

I suppose something I could do is to eliminate all narrative/reasoning portions from this concept and only put down what he is and what he is capable of doing.

That would be the opposite of progress here.

There isn't really a section in the template for SCP Abilities.

Correct. There is a reason for this. SCPs are not merely strange things with lists of abilities, they are stories.

+ my suggestion for where to go from here
- Chisel until the parts that don't look like a statue are gone.

First things first, pitfall wise, you're 100% looking at walking a tightrope over Edgelord Canyon here. This guy could easily tip over into the abyss of edgy 90's comic book characters that have names spelled with statistically disproportionate quantities of "x"s and "y"s… but if you can make this guy a rounded, grounded character it could actually work.

I can see a glimmer of raw diamond here, but the gem metaphor applies heavily: the jeweler's task is all about precisely cutting away the extraneous material to leave only the most interesting parts.
Reading through what you've said so far, I spot the makings of a viable elevator pitch that makes my ears perk up-

  • "He doesn't see someone's destiny. He sees their "supposed" destiny, or what it is that they were meant to do in life, the thing that they are driven towards or driven to do."
  • "wears an assortment of anomalous artifacts that are melded with his body."
  • Jack is a part of Twist's mind
  • the general idea of him pursuing a greater, possibly even benevolent, goal in this hunt he's on

The first one is all the anomaly you need to set you up with an interesting character: A guy with a simple but potent ability chasing pieces of a domino chain that could lead to a cataclysmic end scenario that isn't necessarily going to happen.

Not necessarily suggesting any direct/overt connection, but I immediately jump to SCP-4239- (one of the GAW's Misters Against Weed, Mr. Destiny). His anomaly enables people to find their destiny in this exact sense- not a predetermined fate, but rather their driving purpose and their potential for doing the right thing at the right time to set further things in motion. Mostly just pointing it out as an interesting opposite thematically, but there's also big-picture potential for them to at least have intersecting interests at some point.

But back to the current idea: to riff off of what Cybersquid said, the interest here for me lives in that ambiguous intersection and contrast of "Twist is a ruthless murderer chasing shadows that might only exist in his own head" and "Twist is an anti-hero who will stop at nothing to prevent the destruction of the world". He's not an all-knowing unstoppable monster… just a man who sees a little more than others, with an obsession that may or may not be justified, and a few tricks up his sleeve.

Regarding the grab bag of grafted-on anomalies, the bootleg cyborg thing is a vibe I'm personally a fan of in general, but in this case keep it grounded. A laundry list of abilities isn't going to interest the audience, and pulling out a new gadget every two minutes to do exactly whatever he wants is cartoon supervillain territory. Use simple things in a clever way, though and you paint a picture of a resourceful and competent threat building on past successes.

You've got a great way to organically tie this part of his concept back into the rest, making it even more interesting and playing up that "magnificent bastard" aspect at the same time: What if he can see the potential in things, too? You could get a ton of milage out of having most of his collection being the sort of thing you'd see on the Anomalous Items List, combined in clever ways because he can see their potential. This can complicate his moral standing in odd ways, too- say, he knows that item A vastly increases his ability to stop the cataclysm, but item A is a piece of paratech in the head of a particular unimportant CotBG member. It's nothing special, but it has to be that one.

More flashy components could also be used to hint at past exploits, or even as the basis for tales in themselves. One suggestion I'd throw out is that SCP-748-5 instances (I won't spoil the non-essential details) have integrated phasing tech- the catch being that their tech self-destructs on termination so the unit would have to be alive functional during the transplant process, and that it's probably not going to be the most stable item in his kit even if both he and the device survive the process.

Lastly, while the "tightrope over Edgelord Canyon" warning remains the big flashing red danger sign here, I'd strongly recommend embracing the edginess a little bit if you go the tale series route- like there's some great potential for zombie-stomping action-horror here if you can keep it on the rails in the process.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I suppose something I could do is to eliminate all narrative/reasoning portions from this concept and only put down what he is and what he is capable of doing.

+ show block
– hide block

Ok, so here's the problem I'm having right now with this particular project. I'm trying to stay within the template and within the word count. I'm trying not to reveal too much information because if I do, it might seem like a big mess or too much information for someone to swallow in one sitting. The James Devillian Twist SCP project is a big project. I mean… a very big project. He has a wide array of other anomalous abilities and somewhat complicated motivations. He doesn't see someone's destiny. He sees their "supposed" destiny, or what it is that they were meant to do in life, the thing that they are driven towards or driven to do. He sees this along with a ton of other information about that object, including any weaknesses they hold. Twist is a psychopath who will always know how to put his target down.

I read through 049. One major difference here is that through experimentation and interrogation, Twist's "LLUN" threat is verifiable and the second difference is its not a disease. Twist just thinks that if he introduces a small bit of the LLUN's nature to the world, that it might be able to prepare for the upcoming apocalyptic battle with the LLUN, similar to how a vaccine works in a way.

Should I do away with the template and try my own thing with presenting this concept? Use my own format? There isn't really a section in the template for SCP Abilities.

Twist is surrounded in what he calls a “LLUN” aura, which gives Twist his anomalous nature and various abilities and is what prevents Twist from speaking certain truths.

Sorry to be blunt, but what does this mean? I kept thinking it would get unpacked in one of the other sections but it doesn't.

Moreover, I don't see a connection between this aspect, the "deep secret" and the whole vaccine thing… Feels like a few thin ideas sorta slammed together without connective tissue.

James Devillian Twist will instantly uncover this kind of information simply by looking at these creatures. Twist will instantly know various bits of information about a target within his line of sight such as the target's purpose(supposed destiny), function, how it works, and how to eliminate it.

I assume this is from the Aura but that isn't any better connected to these other factors I mentioned above. I think you need to sit down and simplify, make a cohesive anomaly about the one man and focus on his anomalous aspects that thematically connect to each other.

Mostly I think this person's anomalous abilities aren't super interesting (knowing someone's destiny? What does that mean?) but primarily you need to make these different concepts work together or snip some of them.

My suggestion would be to cut the "vaccine" bit as it sounds a little too like SCP-049 without much to differentiate it.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Ok, I have edited the post based on your feedback.

+ show block
– hide block

I wasn't really sure of what singular part of his name to call him. I suppose I could stick with Twist.

Originally, I thought it best to put down the introduction to his story to build intrigue rather than blatantly put down the entirety of what I plan to do for the article. I had put down a lot more information earlier but that exceeded the word count limit.

The core concept of this character does not lie with hunting down and killing Jack. That's just how Twist ended up being discovered. It's what happens after the SCP foundation gets a hold of Twist that makes up what this article is about. Jack is a part of Twist's mind and is Twist's motivation for escaping the foundation. Take him out of the equation and Twist is very cooperative, answering questions and participating in experiments when allowed. While the SCP foundation's involvement prior to his capture is extremely minimal, the article isn't about the capture so much as it is about the SCP foundation's attempts at containing Twist and learning from him.

The LLUN aura is the source of Twist's anomalous nature and is what gives Twist his various abilities. It is designed to be a mystery for readers to uncover upon reading the article and subsequent experimentation/interview logs.

One of Twist's abilities is his ability to look at something and instantly obtain information about that something's purpose, function, how it works, and how to eliminate it. The LLUN aura prevents Twist from divulging information about anything that might reveal information about the LLUN. It is the main antagonizing force within this article as the SCP foundation struggles to get as much information out of Twist as possible, seeing as Twist can contain secret knowledge about ANY SCP creature that he comes into contact with.

The story is about discovery and how much information can actually be obtained with the obstacle of the LLUN aura.

what is the LLUN aura?

After trying and failing to save Jack from Twist, the SCP agents will be surprised to see that Devillian

not a critique per se but a comment: it'd be a lot less confusing if you were consistent with how you refer to James Devillian Twist here; sometimes calling him Twist and sometimes Devillian makes it seem like he's two people.

I don't hate this conceptually, or the idea of like, Twist as this weird extra-reality assassin endlessly hunting down Jack; but my concern is that there's not a lot of context for why: it feels almost like set dressing here because I don't really know who Jack is, or why Twist wants to kill him and so I don't really have feelings on this because I don't know if this is like "Twist is a ruthless murderer who cannot be stopped" or "Twist is the good guy who will stop at nothing to prevent Jack destroying the world".

I'm also extremely conflicted because a lot of this plot feels like it'd work best as a tale centred around one of them repeating the mission over and over again, especially since the Foundation involvement here seems to be uh completely minimal? They appear at some point, do some interviews/experiments with uncertain purpose and outcome and then the story ends, and it feels…underwhelming. Especially when compared to like, the possibility of doing this intense action thing about Twist hunting Jack.

item.title: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
SCP Article
Experimentation, Mystery, (Cross-link required)
Basic article template, followed by a test log section.
Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

James D. Twist is a deformed humanoid male with anomalous objects melded into his body, who brings tidings of extra-dimensional Armageddon. He suffers from frequent migraines and can see into the soul and/or essence of any target he looks at, alive or inanimate, giving him insight into random facts about the target such as its purpose, drive, desire, function, or method of elimination. What aspects he sees about the target depend on the target itself. His own immediate hume levels are unstable, causing various aspects about himself, such as his strength, speed, durability, wit, linguistic ability, etc. to fluctuate.


Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ show block
– hide block

Twist, a collector of anomalous artifacts, utilizes his ability in conjunction with the items he collects in order to create a vast array of unexpected effects. In his mission to prepare humanity for the upcoming crisis, Twist seeks to educate the SCP foundation in some of the horrors that he has had to endure and in what he feels must be done to combat the insanity that is making its way to their reality.


Central Narrative:
+ show block
– hide block

Twist, upon being discovered by the SCP foundation, willingly goes with the foundation to answer their questions. Twist allies with the foundation in order to complete his objective in preparing humanity for possibly its greatest confrontation yet. During his crusade, Twist also uses his ability to uncover insight about various people in the foundation in an attempt to manipulate them to gain access to the foundation's other anomalies.
